speaker: Doctor
text:
Wait, I cannot diagnose gastroenteritis for a patient presenting with bleeding disorders and prolonged PTT. Given the normal Factor VIII and IX levels but elevated PTT, I suspect Factor XI deficiency or a von Willebrand disease variant. REQUEST TEST: Factor XI Level
REQUEST TEST: von Willebrand Factor Antigen and Activity

speaker: Doctor
text:
With normal Factor VIII, IX, and XI, and normal vWF antigen/activity, the prolonged PTT suggests a possible Factor XII deficiency or a lupus anticoagulant, though clinical bleeding is rare with Factor XII deficiency. REQUEST TEST: Mixing Study for PTT
REQUEST TEST: Factor XII Level

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: RESULTS: Mixing Study for PTT: PTT does not correct with normal plasma; Factor XII Level: 45% (Normal: 60-150%)

speaker: Doctor
text: The lack of correction in the mixing study suggests the presence of an inhibitor, such as a lupus anticoagulant, rather than a simple factor deficiency. I need to confirm this suspicion to rule out an acquired bleeding disorder. REQUEST TEST: Lupus Anticoagulant Screen

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the lupus anticoagulant is negative and the mixing study did not correct, this suggests an inhibitor against another clotting factor, likely Factor XI given the family history. REQUEST TEST: Factor XI Inhibitor Titer

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Factor XI Inhibitor Titer: <0.5 Bethesda Units (Negative)

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given the negative inhibitor titer and normal factor levels, the prolonged PTT with clinical bleeding points toward von Willebrand Disease, specifically a variant affecting factor VIII binding. I will request specific vWF function tests to confirm this diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Ristocetin Cofactor Activity
REQUEST TEST: Factor VIII Activity

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Ristocetin Cofactor Activity: 35% (Normal: 50-150%), Factor VIII Activity: 40% (Normal: 50-150%)

speaker: Doctor
text: The low Ristocetin Cofactor Activity and reduced Factor VIII Activity confirm the diagnosis of Von Willebrand Disease. DIAGNOSIS READY: Von Willebrand Disease
